summary_paragraph: The patient, a woman with a complex history including fibrosing mesenteritis, recurrent partial bowel obstructions, and chronic GI dysmotility, was admitted for recurrent nausea, vomiting, and abdominal pain. Imaging confirmed a partial small bowel obstruction, managed conservatively with NPO status, G-tube to gravity, IV fluids, and pain control. G-tube output decreased from over 1200 cc/day to 500–600 cc/day. She received IV iron for iron deficiency anemia and was started on TPN on hospital day 3. Abdominal massage recommended by GI helped stimulate bowel motility, leading to passage of gas and significant pain improvement. She was transitioned to a full liquid diet on day 4, tolerated it well, and was discharged on day 5. Pain management was transitioned from IV morphine to oral MS Contin and liquid morphine for breakthrough pain. She remained ambulatory throughout and was discharged home in good condition with instructions to continue full liquids and Miralax for one week.
